Sandomierz New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sandomierz, Poland

Not demolished. This is the newer of Sandomierz's two Jewish cemeteries, established around 1830, a companion to the Old cemetery documented elsewhere in this collection. During WWII, the Germans dismantled its wall, took tombstones for construction, and carried out mass executions and burials here; in 1944, some bodies were exhumed and burned on the spot in furnaces. After the war, the surviving Jewish Committee, active until 1948, reburied victims exhumed from outside the cemetery and erected a pyramid-shaped monument. In 1956, the government fenced the monument's section while the rest of the cemetery was built over with a school. About 400 matzevot survive, the oldest dated 1848.
